old: D is the tempting one, since tame members being "less fertile" sounds like a real obstacle. But less fertile still means fertile. The tame animals still have offspring, so the program just takes longer, and the conclusion only says domestication is possible "in principle." D would work only if tame members couldn't reproduce at all.
new: D tells us tame members are less fertile than wild members, but it does not tell us whether they can still reproduce. If they can, lower fertility may only make selective breeding slower. C gives a more direct objection: some species have no tame members to select in the first place.
reason: Comparative less fertile does not entail nonzero fertility; remove unsupported assertion while keeping selection gap clear.
